# idfkit

An EnergyPlus IDF and epJSON toolkit for Python, with no third-party dependencies.

[idfkit](https://idfkit.com) · [Developers](https://developers.idfkit.com) · [EnergyPlus docs](https://docs.idfkit.com) · [Envelop](https://app.idfkit.com) · [MCP](https://mcp.idfkit.com) · [Shoebox](https://shoebox.idfkit.com) · [GitHub](https://github.com/idfkit)

[![Release](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/idfkit)](https://pypi.org/project/idfkit/) [![Build](https://github.com/idfkit/idfkit/actions/workflows/main.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/idfkit/idfkit/actions/workflows/main.yml) [![Coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/idfkit/idfkit/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/idfkit/idfkit) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/idfkit/idfkit)](https://github.com/idfkit/idfkit/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Parity](https://img.shields.io/badge/parity-tier%201-blue)](https://developers.idfkit.com/parity/)

> [!NOTE]
> A callout that used to sit above the heading now sits below the badge row.

## Install

```bash
pip install idfkit
```

A fenced block may carry what looks like a heading:

```text
# not a heading
```

## Parity

idfkit and idfkit-js implement one vocabulary. The current parity tier is stated on the
[capability parity page](https://developers.idfkit.com/parity/).
